title: Forgot password and email verification on POST /users
summary: Extended POST /users with forgot_password, reset_password, verify_email, and resend_verification actions. Verification and reset tokens are HMAC-SHA256 hashed at rest with expiry, emails are queued without logging secrets, and forgot/resend responses are generic to prevent account enumeration.

threats_mitigated.description: Distinct responses for known vs unknown emails reveal which accounts exist.
threats_mitigated.mitigation_applied: forgot_password and resend_verification always return the same generic 200 message whether or not a matching user exists.

threats_mitigated.threat_name: Verification or reset token theft from database
threats_mitigated.description: Storing raw tokens in SQLite would expose active reset/verification links on DB compromise.
threats_mitigated.mitigation_applied: Tokens are generated with secrets.token_urlsafe; only HMAC-SHA256 hashes keyed by SECRET_KEY are persisted; tokens cleared after use.

threats_mitigated.description: Long-lived or reusable tokens allow delayed account takeover or email verification bypass.
threats_mitigated.mitigation_applied: verification tokens expire in 24h, reset tokens in 1h; successful verify/reset nulls stored hashes; hmac.compare_digest used on validation.

threats_mitigated.threat_name: Token or credential leakage via logs and email metadata
threats_mitigated.description: Logging reset/verification tokens or password material would expose secrets to operators.
threats_mitigated.mitigation_applied: EMAIL_OUTBOX records only kind and recipient; raw tokens captured only when CAPTURE_EMAIL_TOKENS=1 for tests; no tokens in HTTP responses.

threats_mitigated.threat_name: SQL injection on token and email lookups
threats_mitigated.description: Untrusted email or token values concatenated into SQL could read or mutate user rows.
threats_mitigated.mitigation_applied: All lookups and updates use parameterized ? placeholders.

threats_mitigated.description: SQLite exceptions in responses could leak schema or query details.
threats_mitigated.mitigation_applied: Catch sqlite3.Error and return generic JSON errors with correlation IDs.

best_practices_achieved: Cryptographically random opaque tokens for verification and password reset
HMAC-SHA256 hashed token storage with server secret pepper
Time-bounded token expiry with single-use invalidation after success
Generic responses on forgot-password and resend-verification to resist enumeration
email_verified flag exposed via serialize_user whitelist
Registration automatically queues verification email when email is provided
Parameterized SQL for all new email and token code paths
Automated tests for verification, reset, enumeration resistance, and login after reset

secure_code_snippets.explanation: Reset and verification tokens are validated with constant-time digest comparison and expiry checks.

secure_code_snippets.code:
def forgot_password(data):
    row = conn.execute("SELECT id, email FROM users WHERE email = ?", (email,)).fetchone()
    if row is not None and row["email"]:
        token = issue_reset_token(conn, row["id"])
        conn.commit()
        send_password_reset_email(row["email"], token)
    return jsonify({"message": "If that email is registered, a password reset link has been sent."}), 200
secure_code_snippets.explanation: Password reset requests return the same message regardless of whether the email exists.

guardrails_applied.title: Use modern password hashing and step-up MFA
guardrails_applied.instruction: Use Argon2id/bcrypt/scrypt with per-user salt and tuned work factors; require MFA for privileged actions.
guardrails_applied.notes: reset_password re-hashes new passwords with bcrypt; MFA out of scope.

guardrails_applied.title: Do not build queries or commands with string concatenation
guardrails_applied.instruction: Don't concatenate untrusted input into SQL/NoSQL/LDAP/OS command templates. Use parameterized APIs and safe query builders.
guardrails_applied.notes: Email and token lookups use ? parameter binding.

guardrails_applied.title: Validate and canonicalize all untrusted input server-side
guardrails_applied.instruction: Use allowlists, strict schemas, and length/type/range checks for all request data, file metadata, headers, and external API payloads.
guardrails_applied.notes: Email, password, token, and action fields validated before processing.

guardrails_applied.title: Do not return verbose internal errors to users
guardrails_applied.instruction: Don't expose stack traces, SQL errors, framework debug pages, or internal identifiers in responses. Return generic errors with correlation IDs.
guardrails_applied.notes: Database failures return generic messages with correlation_id.

guardrails_applied.title: Do not expose secrets in source, logs, or error messages
guardrails_applied.instruction: Don't hardcode credentials, include secrets in stack traces, or log tokens/keys/session IDs; load secrets from managed secret stores.
guardrails_applied.notes: Tokens never logged in normal mode; EMAIL_OUTBOX excludes token values.

guardrails_applied.title: Log security-relevant events with integrity and retention controls
guardrails_applied.instruction: Log authentication, authorization failures, and admin actions with actor, target, outcome, and timestamp; protect logs from tampering.
guardrails_applied.notes: Registration, verification, reset request/completion logged by user_id without tokens.

guardrails_applied.title: Use constant-time comparison and expiry for single-use account tokens
guardrails_applied.instruction: Hash account-recovery and email-verification tokens at rest; validate with hmac.compare_digest; enforce TTL and invalidate after successful use.
guardrails_applied.notes: HMAC-SHA256 storage, 1h reset / 24h verification TTL, tokens cleared on success.
